title: Choosing an Architecture Under Constraints
context: A hospital is launching a new patient records platform. Data must remain in the country, and an HVAC control system must stay isolated. You arbitrate the architecture in three decisions.

n1.text: First constraint: patient records must not leave the national jurisdiction. Which criterion drives the choice?

choices.text: Data sovereignty: local hosting or sovereign cloud
choices.why: Data sovereignty is a business criterion that overrides cost when required by law.

choices.text: Encryption at rest, regardless of location
choices.why: Encryption protects confidentiality, but does not satisfy a legal residency requirement.
Cost cannot override a regulatory constraint.

n2.text: IT wants to host the application in the cloud but keep the database on-premises. Which model does this describe?

choices.text: Hybrid model, with a VPN/federated identity junction to secure
choices.why: The hybrid model combines both worlds; the junction becomes a distinct trust zone.
The database stays on-premises: it is not a pure public cloud.
The cloud application rules out total physical isolation.

n3.text: The HVAC system (OT) must remain inaccessible from the Internet. Which decision is safest?

choices.text: Isolated OT network and physical segmentation, controlled transfers, no active scanning
choices.why: In OT, availability and safety come first: strong isolation and passive inspection.

choices.text: Expose OT behind a simple admin password
choices.why: A password does not replace network separation.

choices.text: Run an active vulnerability scan every night on OT
choices.why: An active scan can disrupt equipment that controls physical processes.

n4.outcome: You arbitrated on sovereignty, secured the hybrid junction, and isolated OT without compromising its availability.

debrief: Data sovereignty is a business criterion that can dictate the hosting model.
A hybrid model shifts risk to the on-premises / cloud junction.
OT requires isolation and gentle analysis: availability takes precedence over convenience.
